newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan shilling, inflation ease in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan shilling, inflation ease in 1996.

text.p: The Uganda shilling and inflation on average eased in the calendar year 1996 compared to 1995, the central Bank of Uganda (BOU) said on Thursday.
The bank said that the first half of 1996 saw upward shilling mobility while the latter half saw a depreciation due to shortage of foreign exchange.
The shilling rose over the last two months of 1996 due to the coffee inflows and the presence of a Canadian-led U.N. Multinational Force meant to intereve in eastern Zaire.
The force closed its operations at end-December 1996.

The BOU said the monthly average interbank rate reached a peak of 1,105.5 shillings per dollar in October 1996 versus 1,023.25 per dollar in December 1995. Independant Forex Bureau rates peaked at 1,104.62 per dollar in October 1996.
BOU intervened continuously in the foreign exchange market in 1996 "in order to smoothen flactuations in the market."
The central bank bought a net amount of $7.5 million in December 1996 down from $10.85 million in November 1996.
Gross sales amounted to $125.08 million as compared to $128.95 million over the same period.
The decline was blamed on the scaling down of the U.N. force for Zaire, whose expenditure per month was $1.565 million in food, accommodation and other expenses.

The report said that gross transaction volumes in interbank market rose with purchases topping $1.36 billion in 1996 up from $1.19 billion in 1995. Sales also increased to $1.33 billion from $1.2 billion in 1995.

December 1996 saw the annual headline inflation rate fall to 5.4 percent down from 6.3 percent in November 1996. The annual underlying inflation also declined from 6.4 percent to 5.5 percent during the same period, the central bank said.
It said the significant drops were in food items, beverages, tobacco, clothing, footwear, household and personal goods.

The base money in 1996 rose by from 288.46 billion shillings in 1995 to 323.64 billion in 1996. The rise was blamed on increased credit to the commercial banks by BOU and increased central bank intervention in the foreign exchange market.

The bank said demand deposits in commercial banks grew by from 204.2 billion to 224.5 billion between December 1995 and October 1996. Time and savings deposits also increased by 39 percent from 148.1 billion to 205.8 billion.
In the treasury bill market, the rates rose throughout the year "mainly due to the tight monetary policy stance".

All annualised rates rose in the month of December compared to November 1996. The end-month profile stood at 14.01 percent for 91-day bills, 14.28 percent for 182-days, 14.62 percent for 270-day and 15.24 percent for 364 days versus 13.9. 14.26, 14.10 and 14.40 percent respectively at the end of November, 1996.

Coffee suffered a decline because of a fall in international coffee prices during 1996. Indicative prices for Robusta coffee remained generally below the $2 per kg level throughout 1996 as compared to an average of $3 per kg in 1995.
Farm gate prices for December 1996 declined to a range of 350-400 shillings per kg for robusta coffee down from the 400-500 November range.
